lessons.title: The Russian Nesting Doll
lessons.content_md:
# The Russian Nesting Doll 🪆

Have you ever seen a Russian nesting doll? You open the big wooden doll, and inside is a smaller doll. Open that one, and there's an even smaller doll inside!

In the Cloud, we do this exact same trick with computers. We put **computers inside of computers**.

## The Hardware Problem

Imagine a massive, super-powerful server in a Data Center. It has 128 processor cores and 2,000 Gigabytes of RAM. It's an absolute beast.

If you want to host a tiny website, putting it alone on this massive server is a huge waste! It's like renting a giant 10-bedroom mansion for just one person.

So, how do cloud companies like Amazon or Google share this giant server among hundreds of different customers? They use **Virtual Machines (VMs)**.

<flipcard front="🪆 What is a Virtual Machine?" back="A Virtual Machine is a software computer running inside a physical computer. It acts exactly like a real computer, but it's completely made of code!"></flipcard>

lessons.title: The Hypervisor: The Grand Illusionist
lessons.content_md:
# The Hypervisor: The Grand Illusionist 🎩

If you have a giant physical server, and you want to run 10 smaller Virtual Machines inside of it, you need a special kind of magic. That magic is called a **Hypervisor**.

## Slicing the Pie 🥧

A Hypervisor is a special piece of software that gets installed directly onto the giant physical server.

Its only job is to take the physical resources (CPU, RAM, Hard Drive) and slice them up into smaller pieces, handing them out to the Virtual Machines.

- VM #1 thinks it is a real computer with 4 CPUs and 8GB of RAM.
- VM #2 thinks it is a real computer with 2 CPUs and 4GB of RAM.

The Hypervisor is the illusionist. It makes every VM believe it is a completely independent, physical computer. 

## Absolute Isolation 🛡️

The most important job of the Hypervisor is **Isolation**. If Customer A's virtual machine gets a virus, or crashes entirely, it will **not** affect Customer B's virtual machine running right next to it on the exact same physical server!

<flipcard front="🎩 What is a Hypervisor?" back="A Hypervisor is the software that creates and manages Virtual Machines. It slices up the physical server's resources and keeps the VMs perfectly isolated from each other."></flipcard>
